Facet a plot by one or two variables

Source: R/layout.R
facet.Rd

Splits a plot into small multiples, one panel for each value of rows, cols, or both. Panels share their axes unless free_scales lets them vary.

With both rows and cols, panels form a grid, as in ggplot2's facet_grid(): column labels go in a strip across the top and row labels in a strip down the right side. With rows alone, panels stack in one column with their labels on the right. With cols alone, or with wrap, panels wrap into rows with each label in a strip on top.

Shared axes are drawn once, on the outer panels: the y axis on the left column and the x axis on the bottom row. A strip shows the value alone, such as "4", unless labeller gives another label. Strip font size, weight and colours are theme tokens (see theme_tokens()).

Usage

facet(
  spec,
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  free_scales = "none",
  wrap = NULL,
  labeller = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

A glyph_spec

rows

Row faceting variable: a bare column name, a computed expression (e.g. factor(cyl)), or NULL

cols

Column faceting variable: a bare column name, a computed expression, or NULL

free_scales

"none", "x", "y", "both"

wrap

If only one variable, wrap into a grid with this many columns

labeller

The labels shown in the strips, similar to ggplot2::labeller(). One of:

  • a named character vector, such as c("4" = "Four cylinders"), which looks up each value by its name. Values not in the vector keep their own label.

  • a function that takes the values as a character vector and returns their labels, one for each.

  • a list with one of the above per faceting variable, named as the variable is written in rows or cols, such as list(cyl = c("4" = "Four"), gear = function(x) paste(x, "gears")). Variables not in the list keep their own labels.

Value

Modified glyph_spec

Examples

p <- glyph(mtcars, x = wt, y = mpg) |> mark_point()

# Columns by gear in a strip on top, rows by cyl in a strip on the right.
p |> facet(rows = cyl, cols = gear)
#> <glyph_spec: 32 x 11, 1 mark(s)>

# One variable: panels wrap, with labels on top.
p |> facet(cols = cyl, wrap = 3)
#> <glyph_spec: 32 x 11, 1 mark(s)>

# Relabel some values with a named vector. 8 keeps its own label.
p |> facet(cols = cyl, labeller = c("4" = "Four cylinders", "6" = "Six cylinders"))
#> <glyph_spec: 32 x 11, 1 mark(s)>

# A labeller per variable: a lookup for cyl, a function for gear.
p |> facet(rows = cyl, cols = gear, labeller = list(
  cyl = c("4" = "Four", "6" = "Six", "8" = "Eight"),
  gear = function(x) paste(x, "gears")
))
#> <glyph_spec: 32 x 11, 1 mark(s)>
